extracted.intended_audience: small business founders, startup entrepreneurs, and researchers seeking SBIR/STTR federal funding
extracted.subtask_description: Overview and practical guidance for small businesses applying to the SBIR/STTR (America's Seed Fund) programs, including eligibility, program phases, funding amounts, and basic application steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — small business size
rubrics_metrics.description: I'm a small business with fewer than 500 employees
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program is targeted at small businesses (explicitly stating fewer than 500 employees). This is presented as a primary eligibility question to determine if SBIR/STTR is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit with government missions
rubrics_metrics.description: My company's technology could help support government missions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consider whether their technology addresses federal research and development needs or could support government missions; this is framed as a fit/fit-for-purpose criterion for pursuing SBIR/STTR funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for equity-free funding
rubrics_metrics.description: I'm looking for equity-free funding to develop my ideas
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBIR/STTR awards are described as non-dilutive (the government takes 0% equity or IP ownership), so applicants seeking funding without giving up equity or IP are appropriate candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program purpose and selection focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Fund a portfolio of startups and small businesses across technology areas and markets to stimulate technological innovation, meet Federal R&D needs, and increase commercialization
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program emphasizes (a) stimulating innovation, (b) meeting federal R&D requirements, and (c) increasing commercialization/transition to market. Proposals aligning with these goals are implied to be favored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I — Proof of Concept
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase I: Proof of Concept — 6-12 months, $50,000 - $275,000
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase I supports early proof-of-concept work. Applicants should propose a scope appropriate to a 6–12 month effort and within the $50k–$275k funding range.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase II — Technology Development
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase II: Technology Development — 24 months, $750,000 - $1.8 million
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase II supports advanced technology development. Projects should be scoped for approximately 24 months and funding within the stated $750k–$1.8M range.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase III — Commercialization
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase III: Commercialization — Take your product to the commercial market or sell in the multi-billion dollar federal contracting marketplace
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase III focuses on moving developed technology into commercial markets (private sector or federal contracting). No SBIR/STTR funding ranges are provided for Phase III on this page; the emphasis is on commercialization outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application process steps
rubrics_metrics.description: How To Apply: Identify Opportunities; Apply; Develop Your Idea; Start the Process
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page outlines high-level steps: explore funding opportunities, identify relevant solicitations (with help from supporting organizations), apply (with supporting organizations' help), and develop your idea. It emphasizes that organizations exist to help entrepreneurs through these steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program benefits — equity and IP retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep your equity and IP. 0% Equity or IP ownership taken by the government
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A key benefit highlighted is that awardees retain equity and intellectual property; applicants should expect to keep ownership of their company and IP when funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic and agency participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards given in all 50 states and U.S. Territories; Participating Agencies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBIR/STTR operates across multiple federal agencies and funds companies nationwide (all states and territories). Applicants should expect agency-specific solicitations and national reach.
